title: Flying to Nairobi From Madrid or Barcelona? How Spanish Travellers Plan a Kenya Safari
meta_title: Kenya Safari From Spain, Planned Around August and Easter
meta_description: Plan a Kenya safari from Spain: one-stop flights from Madrid and Barcelona, eTA and health cover, euro budgets and the best months. Quotes from Nairobi.
excerpt: A Kenya safari from Spain in euros: flights from Madrid and Barcelona, the eTA and new health insurance, current Spanish travel advice and three real itineraries.
content:
A Kenya safari from Spain begins with a one-stop flight from Madrid or Barcelona to Nairobi of about 14-16 hours, an online Kenya eTA with compulsory Kenyan health cover, and a private 7-day road safari through Amboseli, the Rift Valley lakes and the Masai Mara. Plan on about €2,600-3,400 per person all in.

Spanish holidays bunch into August, Easter and Christmas, the very weeks when Kenyan lodges and flights cost most. This guide covers routings from Spanish airports, current Spanish travel advice, euro totals for real Kenya safari packages run by our Nairobi team, and timing around the Spanish calendar.

Quick Facts

  • Flights: no nonstop service from Spain to Kenya was listed when we checked in November 2026; one stop, about 14-16 hours door to door
  • Main airports: Madrid-Barajas and Barcelona-El Prat, with Bilbao, Valencia and Palma also connecting
  • Entry: Kenya eTA for Spanish passport holders, from US$30, plus compulsory Kenyan travel health insurance since 5 October 2026
  • Time difference: mainland Spain is 2 hours behind Kenya in winter and 1 hour behind in summer; the Canary Islands are 1 hour further behind
  • Typical budget: about €2,600-3,400 per person for a private 7-day safari or bush-and-beach trip, flights included
  • Best months: July to October for the migration; January to March for dry weather and calm seas on the coast

How Do You Fly From Spain to Kenya?

Every Kenya safari from Spain currently starts with a connection, because no airline was selling a nonstop Spain to Kenya flight when we checked route listings in November 2026. The quickest one-stop options from Barcelona-El Prat and Madrid-Barajas take about 14 h 40 min and 15 h 15 min to Nairobi.

The usual hubs are Amsterdam with KLM, Addis Ababa with Ethiopian Airlines, Abu Dhabi with Etihad, and Istanbul, Doha or Dubai. Many land in Nairobi late in the evening, so on a Kenya safari from Spain we usually plan a first night in Nairobi and start the drive next morning.

Return fares we saw from Spanish airports

Airline route pages listed these lowest return economy fares, taxes included, when we checked in November 2026: KLM from €646 Madrid to Nairobi, €656 from Barcelona and €687 from Bilbao; Ethiopian Airlines from €626 Madrid to Nairobi for January 2027; and Etihad from €579 Madrid to Nairobi for December. Treat them as a floor for a Kenya safari from Spain, since August fares run far higher.

Should you fly into Nairobi or Mombasa?

For a Kenya safari from Spain where the animals are the main event, fly into Nairobi, because Amboseli, Naivasha, Nakuru and the Mara are all reached by road from there. Fly into Mombasa if you want the beach first: Tsavo East is a couple of hours inland, and our 3-day Masai Mara safari from Mombasa flies you from the coast to the reserve and back.

Do Spanish Citizens Need a Visa for Kenya?

Spanish tourists have not needed a visa for Kenya since January 2024, but each traveller on a Kenya safari from Spain, children included, must hold an approved eTA before boarding. The Spanish Foreign Ministry travel advice for Kenya (checked November 2026) says to apply on the official site up to three months ahead and allow three working days.

The official Kenya eTA website lists the fee from US$30 (checked November 2026); you need a hotel booking or our confirmation letter to apply. Since 5 October 2026 visitors must also buy Kenyan travel medical insurance through the eTA site, at about US$44 for a standard stay, and the Spanish ministry notes that foreign policies do not replace it.

That Kenyan cover is only the entry minimum for a Kenya safari from Spain, so keep your own travel insurance for cancellation, luggage and medical evacuation. Our full Kenya eTA guide walks through the form screen by screen.

Is a Kenya Safari From Spain Safe Right Now?

A Kenya safari from Spain on the classic southern circuit is considered safe by the Spanish Foreign Ministry, which advises caution and avoiding specific zones. Its page says there have been no terrorist attacks so far in Kenya's parks and reserves, and that parks outside the risk areas are generally fine with an accredited operator and daytime travel.

The zones it asks Spaniards to avoid lie away from the southern safari routes: the Somali border counties, the coast between the Tana and Galana rivers, the far north, and parts of six North Rift counties, including Baringo, Laikipia and Samburu, under a night curfew. Watamu and Diani are not listed. For Samburu or Laikipia, we check the latest wording first.

The ministry asks travellers to register on its Registro de Viajeros and was last revised in October 2026, so reread it before you fly. Our guide to safety on a Kenya safari covers the practical side.

Vaccines and malaria

No vaccine is compulsory on a Kenya safari from Spain, but you need a yellow fever certificate if you arrive from or transit a risk country; our yellow fever requirements page explains the rule. Malaria is present, especially by Lake Victoria and on the coast, so ask a travel clinic about tablets; NHS Fit for Travel has a country summary (checked November 2026).

The Spanish page also carries an Ebola health notice linked to a WHO emergency declared in May 2026, centred on the Democratic Republic of the Congo, so check it before departure. Our Kenya safari vaccinations guide lists the routine jabs.

What Does a Kenya Safari From Spain Cost in Euros?

A private 7-day Kenya safari from Spain costs about €3,250 per person all in on our classic road route, about €2,580 for the Tsavo and Watamu bush-and-beach trip, and about €3,380 for the Masai Mara and Diani honeymoon by air. A shared 4-day budget safari comes to roughly €1,560.

Our trip prices are in US dollars, converted at the European Central Bank rate of 1 euro to US$1.0963 on 24 November 2026 (ECB euro reference rates). They are planning figures from low-season starting prices; your quote moves with dates and lodge availability.

What pushes the price of a Kenya safari from Spain up?

August costs most on every line, as Spain's main holiday month falls in migration season, and coast prices also rise over Christmas and Easter. The optional Masai Mara balloon flight is US$500 (about €456) per person.

Which Itinerary Suits Travellers From Spain?

Most guests on a Kenya safari from Spain take a 7-day road safari or a week split between the bush and the Indian Ocean, which fits a 10- to 12-day holiday with travel days. Honeymooners usually lean towards the beach split, and first-timers towards Amboseli and the Mara.

Classic road safari: Amboseli, the lakes and the Mara

Our 7-day Amboseli, Naivasha, Nakuru and Masai Mara safari is the route we suggest most often for first-timers. It runs by private Land Cruiser on full board with park fees included: two nights with Amboseli's elephants below Kilimanjaro, a boat ride on Lake Naivasha, a night at Lake Nakuru for rhinos, and three nights in the Mara.

Bush and beach: Tsavo and Watamu

Watamu suits a Kenya safari from Spain with time on the beach, and our Tsavo and Watamu bush and beach safari gets there without backtracking. You drive through Tsavo West and Tsavo East, spend three all-inclusive nights at Turtle Bay Beach Club, then take a short flight from Malindi to Nairobi for your connection home.

The Tsavo route takes in Mzima Springs, the Shetani lava flow and the Ngulia rhino sanctuary, plus snorkelling in Watamu Marine National Park, and it is the best-value week in the cost table.

Honeymoon: the Mara and Diani by air

For a honeymoon, our Masai Mara and Diani honeymoon safari links three nights at Ashnil Mara Camp on the Mara River with three nights at The Sands at Nomad on Diani Beach, using short flights instead of long road transfers. Our Kenya honeymoon safari guide compares other camps and beaches, and couples who prefer Zanzibar can read our Zanzibar beach extension guide.

Diani sits south of Mombasa, and flights from Nairobi land at Ukunda airstrip a few minutes from the hotels. A Kenya safari from Spain in January or February catches dry plains and calm seas together.

When Should You Go, Given Spanish School Holidays?

The best fit for a Kenya safari from Spain is September or October if your work allows it: the migration is usually still in the Mara, Spanish families are back at school and European demand eases. January and February are the other sweet spot, with dry plains, calm seas at Diani and lower rates than August.

Insider Tips for Travellers From Spain

  • Book the eTA early: apply once flights are fixed, within the three-month window, and print the approval
  • Pack for the bush plane: fly-in safaris usually limit you to a soft bag of about 15 kg, so leave the hard suitcase in Nairobi or at the beach hotel
  • Carry US dollars: small, recent notes for tips and park extras; euros are less widely accepted outside Nairobi and the coast
  • Canary Islands departures: allow for the extra hop to Madrid or Barcelona, and an extra hour of time difference on arrival
  • Register your trip: sign up on the Spanish Foreign Ministry's Registro de Viajeros before you leave

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a direct flight from Spain to Kenya?

No direct flight from Spain to Kenya was listed as of November 2026. Travellers from Madrid, Barcelona or Bilbao connect once, usually via Amsterdam, Addis Ababa, Abu Dhabi, Istanbul, Doha or Dubai. The quickest take about 14 to 16 hours in total, and Ethiopian Airlines also sells one-stop fares from Madrid to Mombasa for a beach-first trip.

How much does a Kenya safari from Spain cost?

A Kenya safari from Spain costs about €2,600 to €3,400 per person for a private week, including a return flight of around €650, the eTA, the compulsory Kenyan health insurance and tips. A shared 4-day budget safari is about €1,560 all in. August, Easter and Christmas cost more, and the balloon flight is an extra US$500.

Do Spanish citizens need a visa for Kenya?

Spanish citizens do not need a visa for a holiday in Kenya, but every traveller, including children, needs an approved electronic travel authorisation (eTA) before flying. Apply on the official Kenyan government site up to three months ahead and allow at least three working days. Since October 2026 you must also buy the Kenyan travel health insurance during the process.

What is the best month for a Kenya safari from Spain?

September and October are the best months for a Kenya safari from Spain for most travellers, because the migration is usually still in the Masai Mara and demand from Europe falls after August. January and February are also excellent, with dry weather and calm seas for a beach extension. April and May bring the long rains.

Can I combine a Kenya safari with a beach holiday?

Yes, a Kenya safari combines easily with the beach. Tsavo and Watamu link by road in our 7-day bush and beach trip, while the Masai Mara and Diani link by short flights on our honeymoon itinerary. Many Spanish travellers also add Zanzibar, which is a short flight from Nairobi.

Final Thoughts

A Kenya safari from Spain takes one connection, an eTA with the new Kenyan health cover and a budget of about €2,600-3,400 per person for a private week. Book early for August or Easter, or choose September, October, January or February for quieter parks and better value.
